title: Charles House
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: Framed openings give adjoining rooms a distinct edge while maintaining a view towards the garden. The photograph supports a reading of spatial sequence; the architect's account, rather than this image alone, establishes how rooms can adapt for different generations.

title: Mahogany House
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: The courtyard holds an outdoor table between glazed building edges. It offers a way to study the relationship between separate quarters and a shared setting. This reading does not establish the privacy or access arrangements hidden from the photograph.

title: 3 Generation House
architect: BETA office for architecture and the city
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: The staircase sits directly beside a dining and kitchen area. BETA documents two stacked apartments and provision for changing household arrangements. This interior view explains the presence of circulation in daily life; it does not show the complete independent entrance or lift journey.

title: Veil + Co. House
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: The covered walkway connects separate parts of the house while openings retain control at the building edge. Its value for Together, Apart lies in the combination of shelter, a clear route and recognisable thresholds. Dimensions and accessibility cannot be established from the photograph.

title: La Borda
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: Doors, plants and galleries face a shared internal courtyard. The photograph makes the relationship between a dwelling edge and collective circulation visible. It offers a question for the proposal: how can an occupied entrance sit beside a route that remains available to others?

title: Marmalade Lane
annotation_credit: Analytical overlays: Adam Hingston, 2026. Photo reading, not a measured survey.
note: The lane is framed by housing, planting and low edges used for sitting. The photograph records a shared pedestrian setting, rather than proving how often neighbours interact. For Together, Apart, the useful comparison is between the route through a cluster and the territory immediately beside each home.
